## Deployment groups

The deployment view groups the earlier 42 selected resource/client roles into the locations below. The mapping is explicit in [layers.json](layers.json); grouping does not remove their identities or imply one Pod per group. The CPU disk group adds the shared persistence boundary.

| Location | Selected groups and resources |
|---|---|
| Operator PC | Browser/API client and IAP/SSH forwarding process |
| CPU host loopback | Bounded viewer processes; distinct from NGINX |
| CPU K3s · data/serving | KFP API/task Pods and Spark driver/executors; Feature/Drift APIs, KServe predictor and serving Redis |
| CPU K3s · agents | Controller, UI, catalog, PostgreSQL; coordinator/retrieval/drift WorkerPools; both MCP Deployments |
| CPU K3s · substrate | Six Valkey members and RustFS snapshot volumes; substrate routing/identity controls |
| CPU K3s · inference/edge | llm-d router/EPP; observer and model-control containers; NGINX private gateway; bounded-memory Jaeger |
| CPU Docker | Airflow API/scheduler/DAG processor and DB; DataHub GMS/frontend and stores; MLflow/SQLite/artifacts; Jenkins; Spark/Kafka/Flink and Feast jobs |
| CPU host services | Prometheus, Grafana, Alloy, Loki, Pushgateway, node exporter, Vault and scoped consumers |
| CPU disks | Persistent datasets, registries, CAS, journals, DB/model state; separate SSD scratch; bounded PVC/bind mounts |
| GPU worker · same cluster | One llama.cpp Deployment, one V100, private ClusterIP service, reserved node selector and read-only host model files |

The Feature API seeds a small memory-backed state copy rather than mounting bulk training data. Retrieval MCP copies its own verified knowledge state. GPU model files live on the GPU host. Jaeger is memory-backed and can lose traces on restart. A stopped VM, a retained disk and an unexpired feature lease are different states. Neither same-host replicas/executors nor one GPU establish host-level HA; Recreate can interrupt inference.

## Reading size

The primary system view uses 28px text on a 1,600px canvas (about 15.7px at 896px display width). Flow/deployment text is at least 22px at native size. Use full-resolution PNG/SVG for inspection rather than compressing every implementation detail into the README preview.

Open [architecture.html](architecture.html) from a local clone. The selector groups **Layer 1**, **Layer 2**, **Layer 3** and reference views; it starts with the system architecture. **Read labels** zooms to at least natural width and a minimum 16px text size; scroll inside the canvas. **Fit** restores the full composition. Play/pause, speed and arrow details work offline. Reduced-motion preferences start the viewer paused and select static PNGs in embedded previews. GitHub displays HTML source, so use the local file for interactive controls.

Native screenshots remain original. Before/after Spark captures use one full-width image per row. Separate readable benchmark panels are derived from unchanged native reports, including the slower aggregate dedup candidate.

patches.old: The first dependency/browser installation needs a network connection. Rendering and viewing use local assets and make no platform, model or cloud requests. `export.mjs` uses the pinned Excalidraw 0.18.0 renderer, embeds fonts/logos, and derives every motion path from the native arrow's actual point order. It does not generate the architecture layout. `--write-native` additionally normalizes the edited scenes through Excalidraw and embeds the reviewed icon assets. The verification output must use a new path under `outputs/`.
patches.new: The renderer uses Excalidraw 0.18.0 and derives motion from authored arrow points. It does not invent a layout. Repeat the selected export for each edited view; `preview.mjs --all` reuses byte-identical previews whose source hashes match. Each preview has 36 distinct frames over six seconds and an adjacent source/byte manifest. `DIAGRAM_PYTHON` selects an interpreter with Pillow. Dependencies/browser installation needs a network connection; rendering/viewing makes no platform or model requests.

patches.old: The checker validates native element IDs, bindings, source paths, image assets, dimensions, component/text overlap, routed arrows and all 155 motion paths across ten views. Browser checks exercise every handoff detail, real particle movement, pause/resume, speed, zoom, path clicks, reduced motion, mobile layout and absence of external requests. These are documentation checks, not a fresh workload run or coursework grade.
patches.new: From the repository root, `python -B -S scripts/verify-architecture-layers.py` checks layer membership, source bindings, critical storage/tool/training boundaries, deployment coverage and authored artifact identities. The diagram checker separately validates actual geometry, source paths, native bindings, motion, controls, desktop/mobile behavior and reduced-motion fallbacks. These checks support review; they do not certify a grade or current runtime health.

patches.old: `preview.mjs --all` captures each authored SVG and `encode-preview.py` encodes its 36 frames into a six-second GIF. Use `--view platform-serving` to select one view and `--force` to recapture a previously verified preview. An unchanged source/preview hash is reused byte for byte. Independent staggered phases have arbitrary timing; this does not record an application session. A fixed palette reserves source colors to preserve small product marks. Each adjacent `.preview.json` manifest binds exact GIF bytes and SVG text with CRLF canonicalized to LF. Every embedded preview selects the PNG for reduced-motion visitors. Use `DIAGRAM_PYTHON` if the Python interpreter with Pillow is not named `python`.

patches.old: The [deployment view](../images/platform-deployment.svg) ([Excalidraw source](../diagrams/platform-deployment.excalidraw)) shows 42 selected workload/client resources: the Feature and Drift APIs, each MCP service, controller/UI/catalog, worker pools, router, substrate state, Docker workloads and host processes. Frames group resources by host and runtime; they are not additional services. A WorkerPool can own multiple worker Pods. The observer and turn adapter share one Deployment with two containers. Feast SDK runs inside consuming jobs/APIs. PostgreSQL, the six-member Valkey cluster, RustFS snapshots, Jaeger, the Airflow DAG processor and the DataHub frontend have their own labels. The VM's loopback viewer is separate from NGINX: U1–U3 follow browser access through IAP/SSH to the viewer and its CA/SNI-verified upstream HTTPS connection. G1–G4 show the model request and return. Framework-internal controllers and other supporting databases remain in the source manifests; this is a selected inventory.
patches.new: The [deployment view](../images/deployment-runtime.svg) ([Excalidraw source](../diagrams/deployment-runtime.excalidraw)) groups the selected resources by physical host and runtime. The [deployment crosswalk](../diagrams/README.md#deployment-groups) maps all 42 earlier client/workload roles into these named groups; a group is not one Deployment. The CPU disk group adds the shared persistence boundary. WorkerPools own worker Pods; the observer Deployment contains the observation/turn adapter and model-control containers. Feast executes inside jobs/APIs. The operator's loopback/IAP hop, bounded CPU viewer and CA/SNI-verified HTTPS hop remain separate. G1/G2 show CPU control and GPU response traffic; the GPU worker belongs to the same K3s cluster. Jaeger has bounded in-memory storage. Framework controllers and supporting databases remain in source manifests; this is a selected recorded inventory, not a live status check.
